industrial warehouse in Cabanes (Girona) and seized 8,025 kg of hashish.

of the Gavà instance court. The seven detainees were brought before the

suspect, officers found 36 kg of hashish, a silenced compressed-air rifle and
about 10,000 euros in cash, and arrested the man and a woman on suspicion of

transported drugs; they found 2 kg of cocaine, several doses, cutting substance,
a pistol with 9 mm cartridges and a bow with arrows, plus a hydraulic press
allegedly used to compress cocaine. A further person was arrested as
connected to the case; officers suspect the drugs were distributed to third
parties for small-scale sale, and the investigation remains open, so further
arrests are not ruled out. Agents from the Unidad de Prevención y Reacción,
Grupo II de Estupefacientes and Guías Caninos also took part in the searches.

Katunayake for allegedly attempting to smuggle hashish worth approximately Rs.
51 million into Sri Lanka. The suspects were arrested by officers of the
Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) early on 15 October 2026 while attempting to leave
the airport with the narcotics. The three suspects, aged 22, 22 and 33, are
reportedly employed as drivers in Thailand. They arrived at Katunayake
Airport from Bangkok, Thailand, aboard Thai Airways flight TG-307 at
approximately 12.30 a.m. on 15 October 2026. Newswire reported that
officers discovered 5.96 kilograms of hashish concealed inside cosmetic product
containers in the suspects' three pieces of luggage. Ada Derana reported a
total of 5 kilograms and 96 grams of hashish concealed inside containers of
cosmetic products packed in three pieces of luggage. Daily Mirror reported
that a search of the suspects' luggage uncovered 5 kilograms and 96 grams of
hashish concealed inside cosmetic cream containers in three travel bags.
Sri Lanka Mirror reported that Police Narcotics Bureau officers discovered 5.096
kilogrammes of hashish concealed inside containers of cosmetic products in the
suspects' three pieces of luggage. The three suspects and the seized
hashish are scheduled to be produced before the Negombo Magistrate's Court on 15
October 2026. The Police Narcotics Bureau at Katunayake Airport is
conducting further investigations.

report.title: Appeal halves sentence in Kristiansand hashish smuggling case: 18.566 kg
report.summary: A man in his 40s convicted of smuggling 18.566 kg of hashish through the Kristiansand ferry terminal had his four-year sentence halved to two years by the Agder Court of Appeal. The court found threats against him proven but held it unproven that he knew of 996.7 g of cocaine also hidden in the car.
report.body:
A man in his 40s was convicted to four years in prison after being stopped with
large quantities of narcotics at the Kristiansand ferry terminal, and the Agder
Court of Appeal has now halved his sentence because it was not proven that he
knew about the cocaine in his car. A man in his 40s was stopped by customs
officers at the Kristiansand ferry terminal on 6 November 2025 as he arrived
from Denmark in a German-registered Mazda belonging to his sister. Under
the floor of the boot, the officers found 18.566 kilograms of hashish and 996.7
grams of cocaine. The man admitted smuggling the hashish but denied knowing
that the car also contained cocaine.

Agder District Court convicted him in August 2026 and sentenced him to four
years in prison. He told the court he had borrowed 3,500 euros from a
person in Germany and could not repay the debt. He said he was pressed into
smuggling 15 kilograms of hashish to Norway to clear the debt, and was to
receive 1,000 euros. He told the court that the smugglers threatened him
and his family with violence, on one occasion pointing a pistol at his head and
breaking his little finger. The Court of Appeal accepted that he had been
subjected to serious threats and that his finger was broken. No DNA or
fingerprints from the man were found on the drug packaging, while DNA from three
other persons was detected. The Court of Appeal therefore concluded that it
was not proven beyond reasonable doubt that he had intent to import the cocaine. Even if he had seen the packages, it would not necessarily have been
possible to establish that one of them contained cocaine, the judgment says.

The Court of Appeal held that he should be punished only for importing 18.566
kilograms of hashish, taking a starting point of two years and ten months
reduced for his confession and the threats he faced. The final sentence was
two years in prison, half of the district court's four-year term. The man
was credited with 374 days already spent in pre-trial detention. The Court
of Appeal also noted that he could have contacted the police before crossing the
border and that he stood to gain financially from the smuggling.

report.body:
Immigration police and health officials raided a luxury rental home in Bangkok
and seized over five tons of marijuana buds hidden in a three-story property in
the Bang Khen district. Black trash bags stuffed with cannabis buds were
scattered across all three floors, and officers arrested one Vietnamese national
and four workers from Myanmar. Police suspected the Vietnamese national of
managing the daily operations like a corporate supervisor, while the Myanmar
workers earned 200 to 300 baht per day. The foreign nationals had been
quietly living and working at the location for over a year. Officers spent
two full months investigating the property before moving in to shut down the
illicit business. The raid followed complaints from nearby residents about
a strong, lingering smell of cannabis. The property was fitted with a
custom exhaust pipe system to try to hide the heavy scent.

The operation was ordered by the national police chief and led by the
Immigration Bureau commander. Officers arrested one Vietnamese and four
Myanmar nationals who were sorting the buds to prepare packaging and
distribution to customers. Numerous black bags containing cannabis buds
were hidden throughout all three floors, totaling over 5 tons. The house
had an installed ventilation system designed to expel the odor outside. A
Thai individual had signed the lease agreement before the foreigners moved in
and operated the site for over a year. The Myanmar workers were paid 200 to
300 baht a day to sort and pack the buds. The group held a licence for
cannabis bud processing in Nong Bua Lam Phu province, but their business in
Bangkok was illegal. Violations carry up to one year in prison or a fine of
up to 20,000 baht. The seized cannabis buds were to be sent to a laboratory
to determine whether they were locally grown or imported. Police were
expanding the investigation into possible involvement by additional people from
Myanmar, Vietnam and China.

nine years' imprisonment for illegally growing cannabis and storing narcotic
material for sale. He had grown cannabis on his homestead plot since April
2026, fertilising the soil, weeding and watering the plants. He dried part
of the harvest in the attic and ground and packed another part into glass jars
for storage and, according to the investigation, sale. During the trial he
partially admitted guilt, saying he grew the cannabis only for personal use. The court rejected his claim that the cannabis was intended only for
personal use. The court also took into account that he had previously
served five years' imprisonment for growing cannabis. His brother had to
take out a loan to post the 133,120 hryvnia bail set during the investigation. The verdict has not entered into legal force and may be appealed to the
Mykolaiv Court of Appeal within 30 days.

Police searched his residence on 25 July 2026 and seized 14 cannabis plants and
more than 8 kilograms of cannabis. The police statement reported more than
10 kilograms of dried drug material seized in the same search. He was
detained in July 2026 under Article 208 of the Criminal Procedure Code of
Ukraine. He was notified of suspicion of unauthorised production,
manufacture, acquisition, storage for sale and sale of narcotics in particularly
large sizes and of illegal sowing or growing of cannabis. All seized
material was sent for expert examination. During the pre-trial
investigation a court ordered him held in custody with the possibility of
posting bail.

The Mykolaiv Regional Prosecutor's Office announced the case. The court
imposed no confiscation of property. Officers of police station No. 2 of
the Mykolaiv District Police Department exposed the activity in July 2026.

attempts.decision_title: South Africa cannabis legalisation is a law change
attempts.explanation: The submitted Al Jazeera article reports that President Cyril Ramaphosa signed the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act on 26 May 2024, making South Africa the first African nation to legalise recreational cannabis use, possession and home cultivation. This is a change in the law rather than a single enforcement event such as a raid, seizure, arrest, prosecution, sentence or execution, so it belongs to the Cannabis Freedom Index history rather than the tracker. The article's passing references to earlier events (a 2020 raid on The Haze Club and the number of people imprisoned for cannabis offences as of 2022) are context and are not reported here as enforcement events; they would need their own opened sources. No cannabis quantity, arrest or court outcome is recorded for this submission.
